newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall more with NYMEX late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall more with NYMEX late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes fell further with NYMEX late Wednesday, while California heavies rose, playing catch-up with higher futures from last week, traders said.

Buyers said Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude would be more affordable following the day's $1.04 drop in January futures for West Texas Intermediate crude. High inventories and prospects of further volume from Iraq pressured markets.
ANS dropped 75 cents to $21.55/21.75 a barrel, amid the steep WTI sell-off and flat differentials.
A major producer kept their ANS offer at $1.65 under January WTI, but saw no takers early Wednesday.
A trader said West Coast refiners would likely consider newly returned Iraq crudes.
"If (refiners) loaded some soon, they could have it to the West Coast by the end of January. I'm sure they're taking a real hard look at those (Iraq) numbers before they buy ANS," he said.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said, noting deals done in the posting plus market fell between $0.95 abd $1.05.
Meanwhile, problems at several California refineries left extra heavy grades in spot markets.
Traders said higher inventories and a decrease $0.50 to $1.00 drop in posted prices Wednesday forced companies to lower posted prices.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
Outright prices increased 60 cents to $17.40/17.50 a barrel.
